name: Info Edge (India) Ltd
title: Info Edge (India) Ltd - 532777 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Naukri billings slowed to 10% in FY26 with recruitment hiring stuck in a lukewarm market; Q4 margin held near 58% but 99acres billings grew just 2% after a one-time ₹20.5 cr warranty write-back flattered revenue.

triggers.label: Recruitment billings +9% FY26
triggers.quote: The year was impacted by geopolitical headwinds, tariffs related to uncertainty, and a generally cautious hiring stance amongst corporates

triggers.label: 99acres billings +2% in Q4
triggers.quote: This had a one-time transitional impact on Q4 billings. We expect billings growth to recover in Q1 once again.

triggers.label: Housing/MagicBricks weakening
triggers.quote: There have been leadership changes at both Housing and MagicBricks.

triggers.label: Shiksha billings hit by AI search
triggers.quote: AI -driven changes in search behaviour have been affecting Shiksha's traffic for several quarters.

guidance.value: Double-digit topline growth should keep margins at current level; 7-8% growth may cost some margin
guidance.quote: if we are able to grow our topline in double digits, margins should remain the same

guidance.value: Double billings over 3 years; 25-30% EBITDA margin
guidance.quote: We should aim to at least double our business, if you ask me, over the next 3 years.

guidance.value: Few hundred crores incremental revenue over 3 years
guidance.quote: over a three -year period, it'd be great if we can make a few hundred crores of incremental revenue from these offerings

red_flags.label: Q4 99acres one-time revenue write-back ₹20.5 cr
red_flags.quote: revenue for the quarter as well as for the year stands increased by Rs. 20.5 crores as a result.

red_flags.label: Billings pulled forward/invoicing controls tightened
red_flags.quote: Customers are willing to pay us in advance, and we've sort of clamped down on some of those things.

summary.headline: Info Edge Q4 FY26 standalone billings rose 7% to Rs.1,057 crore and revenue 17% to Rs.805 crore, with 99acres billings flat at 2%.
summary.overview: Standalone operating profit rose 39% YoY to Rs.323 crore at a 40% margin, helped by a one-time Rs.20.5 crore 99acres warranty provision write-back that lifted revenue. Recruitment billings grew 10% standalone (9% including Zwayam and DoSelect) amid a subdued hiring market, with GCCs de-growing 1% in Q4. 99acres billings grew only 2% after a sales reorganisation and tighter invoicing controls, while traffic share rose to 49% web and 52% in April. Management guided to double-digit Naukri topline growth as the threshold for holding margins, and said 99acres should turn cash-generative in FY27 if execution holds.

segments.name: Recruitment (Naukri, standalone)
segments.commentary: Q4 billings Rs.811 crore (+10%), revenue Rs.581 crore (+14%), operating margin 58% on Rs.340 crore profit (+22%). FY26 billings Rs.2,374 crore (+10%), margin 57%; growth stayed in the 9-11% band all year.

segments.name: Naukri JobSeeker Services
segments.commentary: Q4 billings Rs.53 crore (+33%) at 60% margin; FY26 billings Rs.176 crore (+19%) with Rs.98 crore operating profit. Online revenue mix rose from 27% to 53% in 15 months.

segments.name: NaukriGulf
segments.commentary: Q4 billings Rs.41 crore (+9%), down from about 20% growth before Middle East disruption; FY26 billings Rs.126 crore (+16%) at 35% operating margin.

segments.name: 99acres (real estate)
segments.commentary: Q4 billings Rs.163 crore (+2%), revenue Rs.144 crore (+36%) including the Rs.20.5 crore one-time write-back; operating profit Rs.3 crore. FY26 billings Rs.497 crore (+10%), revenue Rs.488 crore (+19%), operating loss Rs.59 crore.

segments.name: Matchmaking (Jeevansathi and Aisle)
segments.commentary: Jeevansathi Q4 billings Rs.39 crore (+21%) with a Rs.3 crore operating loss; Jeevansathi plus Aisle FY26 billings Rs.182 crore (+29%) and combined operating loss halved to Rs.15 crore.

segments.name: Education (Shiksha)
segments.commentary: Q4 billings Rs.45 crore (-13%), revenue Rs.44 crore (+11%), operating profit Rs.6 crore. FY26 billings Rs.164 crore (+1%), revenue Rs.170 crore (+13%); AI-led search changes cut Google referral traffic.

guidance_outlook: Naukri margins: if topline grows 10% or more, margins should hold; faster growth could expand them; growth of 7-8% could cost some margin in the short term.
Continued investment in JobHai and AI; JobHai targeted to grow about 100% YoY for the next few years, with plans to be more aggressive in Mumbai and Bangalore this year.
99acres: expects billings growth to recover in Q1 FY27; medium-term goal to double billings over 3 years and reach 25-30% EBITDA margin, with cash generation in FY27 if all goes well.
Shiksha: AI-led search headwind expected to persist near term; counselling and voicebots expected to progressively offset it.
Deferred revenue: billings slowdown in H2 FY26 will flow through to lower revenue growth in FY27, per management.
Long-term aspiration: AI-Rex, Talent Pulse, PremiumX and related offerings could add a few hundred crore rupees of incremental revenue over three years.
capex_capacity: 99acres: traffic share rose to 49% web in Q4 FY26 from 46%, 54% app traffic share, and 51% overall in March and 52% in April 2026.
99acres new projects market estimated at Rs.5,000-5,500 crore; new-home responses grew 33% YoY in Q4 versus 20-22% last year; 99Shorts rolled out in NCR with other cities planned for FY27.
AI-Rex agentic recruiting platform: over 1,000 clients onboarded and about 30,000 job mandates processed; made free to many recruiters to drive adoption.
Naukri resumes database about 115 million; about 21,000 resumes added per day in Q4 FY26.
Info Edge Ventures: over 130 non-strategic investments since 2007, about 50 deep-tech or AI-first; two new funds (growth stage and deep tech) launched.
demand_pricing: Hiring sentiment described as lukewarm; JobSpeak Index grew 7-8% YoY in FY26 and has been stable in a 4-6% range per management.
Q4 recruitment billings by segment: Tech, IT and BPM +6%; GCCs -1%; recruitment consultants +8%; other sectors +14%. FY26: Tech/IT/BPM +8%, GCCs +10%, consultants +6%, other sectors +8%.
IT services are 19% of billings (grew 10% in FY26); other sectors are 29% of billings (grew 8% in FY26 vs 14% in FY25).
Premium hiring (above Rs.25-30 lakh) growing faster than mid-level; LinkedIn seen as stronger for senior and passive candidates.
B2C jobseeker revenue growing about 30% after self-serve shift, versus 18-20% historically; paid users rose from 1.2% to 2.2% of MAU in 15 months.
99acres competitors: MagicBricks, Housing (burn about Rs.250 crore per year), NoBroker; Meta and Google compete in new homes; management said leadership changes at Housing and MagicBricks.
Q4 99acres billings hit by a one-time transitional impact from sales reorganisation and tighter invoicing controls on advance collections.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hiring sentiment across GCCs, IT and non-IT, and what is driving 99acres margins and share gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Hitesh Oberoi called the market lukewarm; larger GCCs have shrunk headcount while smaller ones hire. Share gains credited to execution, with 13-14 points added to traffic share in recent months; new-home responses up 33% in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs.20 crore 99acres revenue write-back sustainable, and how did it affect billings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was a one-time reversal of over-provisioned warranty on cost-per-lead products, which did not affect billings. Provision will move from 20% to 5% of leads going forward; the write-back was not expected to recur.

qa_highlights.question: Why did jobseeker services revenue grow so fast, and is there guidance for it?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth came from AI tools, a self-serve shift away from telecalling and a counter-cyclical lift as hiring slowed. Management was surprised by 30% growth after one quarter and said it was unsure whether it would sustain.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for JobHai and its monetisation model?
qa_highlights.answer: The model is similar to Apna and WorkIndia but more freemium. It is monetising in Delhi NCR and will expand to Mumbai and Bangalore; management targets about 100% YoY growth for several years.

qa_highlights.question: How should margins and 99acres growth be framed for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Naukri margins hold at 10%+ topline growth; 99acres aim is 60% share, doubling billings in 3 years and reaching 25-30% EBITDA margin. Management said Q1 should recover but near-term markets may slow.

qa_highlights.question: What is the adoption and willingness to pay for AI-Rex, and how does 99acres gain share in new homes?
qa_highlights.answer: AI-Rex was made free to many recruiters after B2B sales friction; it has 30,000 mandates, with 1% take rate targeted. New-home share gains come from secondary-market traffic plus 99Shorts video content.

risks_watch: 99acres Q1 FY27 billings recovery after the 2% Q4 growth and the sales reorganisation; the one-time write-back will not repeat.
Recruitment growth held at 9-11% all year; watch whether Naukri can hold double-digit topline growth to protect the 57-58% margin.
GCC and IT hiring softness, with larger GCCs shrinking headcount and GCCs de-growing 1% in Q4.
Shiksha billings down 13% in Q4 on AI-driven search traffic loss; study-abroad softness in the US and Canada.
Sustainability of B2C jobseeker growth (about 30%), which management said is still unproven after one quarter.
Matchmaking pricing pressure from competitors' discounting; Jeevansathi operating loss of Rs.4 crore in FY26.
summary.management_tone: Confident on 99acres share gains and AI product pipeline, but cautious on the hiring market, which management called lukewarm and stable, and explicit that Q4 billings were a reset. Management was evasive on specific forward numbers, saying near-term outcomes are hard to predict and that the B2C growth may not sustain.
key_quotes: Q4 was a reset. The underlying business trajectory remains intact and we expect growth to recover going forward.

If the Indian economy picks up, we expect the non-IT sectors to start hiring once again, and to start hiring a lot more people than earlier, and attrition rates will pick up, but that'll depend on how the economy plays out over the next few quarters.
If we are able to do that, then we should be able to generate at least a 25 -30% EBITDA margin as well.
This business used to grow at 18-20% per year, but after making these changes, it's now started growing at 30%, but it's only been one quarter.
Now, of course, the team is very bullish, but let's see if this sustains.

growth.why: Management says double-digit Naukri topline growth is needed to hold margins and 99acres should recover in Q1 FY27 with medium-term goal to double billings in 3 years, but no capacity or firm orders back these; the brief also flags billings slowdown in H2 FY26 flowing into lower FY27 revenue growth.
